chapterNote: David's longest thanksgiving, and the one Scripture preserves twice — 2 Samuel 22 records it as the song of his old age, looking back on the day the LORD delivered him from every enemy and from Saul. It opens with a verb no one else in the Bible uses toward God: 'I love You from my depths, O LORD' — racham, a womb-deep, tender love — and then a cascade of titles: crag, fortress, deliverer, God, rock, refuge, shield, horn of salvation, high stronghold. The story is told as a theophany: cords of death and torrents of ruin, a cry from the pit, and then the earth shaking, smoke and fire, the heavens bowed as God comes down riding a cherub on the wings of the wind, darkness His hiding place, hailstones and coals, thunder, arrows of lightning — and the sea floor laid bare at the blast of His nostrils — all so that He could reach down and pull one man out of deep water. The middle of the psalm defends David's integrity, not as sinlessness but as covenant loyalty, and states the law that God is to a man what the man is to Him: faithful to the faithful, pure to the pure, a wrestler to the crooked. Then the arming: hands taught for war, feet like a deer's on the heights, a bronze bow bent, enemies pursued and ground to dust — and the line Christian readers cannot get past: Your gentleness has made me great. The end is Romans 15's proof-text — David giving thanks to the LORD among the nations — and the covenant love promised to David and his seed forever.

1.text: For the choir director. Of David, the servant of the LORD, who spoke the words of this song to the LORD on the day the LORD rescued him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul. He said: I love You from my depths, O LORD, my strength.
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach], A Psalm of David, the servant [ebed] of the LORD [YHWH], who spoke [dabar] unto the LORD the words [dabar] of this song [shir] in the day [yom] that the LORD delivered [natsal] him from the hand [kaph] of all his enemies [oyeb], and from the hand [yad] of Saul [Shaul]: And he said [amar], I will love [racham — love with deep tenderness] You, O LORD, my strength [chezeq].
1.notes: The longest superscription in the Psalter, matching 2 Samuel 22:1: ebed YHWH (H5650), the servant of the LORD. He sings be-yom hitsil YHWH oto (H3117, H5337), on the day the LORD rescued him, mi-kaph kol-oyevav u-mi-yad Shaul (H3709, H341, H3027, H7586), from the palm of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul. Then the verb: erchamkha YHWH (H7355) — the only place in the Bible a man says racham, womb-love, compassion-love, TO God — chizqi (H2391), my strength.

2.text: The LORD is my crag, my fortress, and the One who pulls me free; my God, my rock in whom I take refuge; my shield, the horn of my salvation, my high stronghold.
2.amp: The LORD [YHWH] is my rock [sela — crag, cliff], and my fortress [metsudah], and my deliverer [palat — the one who lets me escape]; my God [El], my strength ['my rock', tsur, the KJV margin], in whom I will trust [chasah — take refuge]; my buckler [magen — shield], and the horn [qeren] of my salvation [yesha], and my high tower [misgab].
2.notes: Eight titles in one breath, most of them geography: sela (H5553), the crag David hid on in the wilderness of Maon; metsudah (H4686), the fortress of Adullam; mephalti (H6403), my escape-maker; tsuri (H6697), my rock; magen, qeren-yishi, misgab (H4043, H7161, H3468, H4869): shield, horn of my salvation, high stronghold. A hunted man's map of his hiding places, every one of them a name for God.

3.text: I call upon the LORD, who is worthy of all praise, and from my enemies I am saved.
3.amp: I will call [qara] upon the LORD [YHWH], who is worthy to be praised [halal]; so shall I be saved [yasha] from mine enemies [oyeb].
3.notes: mehullal eqra YHWH (H1984, H7121): the Praised One is the one I call — the summary of the whole psalm before the story begins. u-min-oyevai ivvashea (H341, H3467), and from my enemies I am saved: the calling and the saving are one sentence.

4.text: The cords of death wrapped around me; the torrents of ruin terrified me.
4.amp: The sorrows [chebel — cords] of death [mavet] compassed [aphaph — encircled] me, and the floods [nachal — torrents, wadis in flood] of ungodly men ['Belial', beliyyaal — worthlessness, ruin, the KJV margin] made me afraid [baath — terrified].
4.notes: chebel-mavet aphaphuni (H2256, H4194, H661): death's ropes closing in — the same cords Psalm 116:3 will sing — and nachale beliyyaal (H5158, H1100), torrents of Belial, the flash-flood wadis of the wilderness as a picture of ruin rushing down. yebaatuni (H1204): terror, not just danger.

5.text: The cords of Sheol were all around me; the snares of death were there to meet me.
5.amp: The sorrows ['cords', chebel, the KJV margin] of hell [sheol] compassed me about [savav]; the snares [moqesh] of death [mavet] prevented [qadam — confronted, came to meet] me.
5.notes: chebel sheol sebabuni (H2256, H7585, H5437), the grave's ropes surrounding; moqeshe mavet qiddemuni (H4170, H4194, H6923) — death's traps came out to MEET him, the old sense of 'prevented': ambush from the front as well as the rear. Verses 4-5 are the pit; verse 6 the cry.

6.text: In my distress I called on the LORD, and to my God I cried for help; from His temple He heard my voice, and my cry came before Him — into His ears.
6.amp: In my distress [tsar] I called [qara] upon the LORD [YHWH], and cried [shava] unto my God [Elohim]: He heard [shama] my voice [qol] out of His temple [hekal], and my cry [shavah] came [bo] before [panim] Him, even into His ears [ozen].
6.notes: ba-tsar-li eqra YHWH (H6862, H7121): in the narrows I called. The answer's path is traced: yishma me-hekhalo qoli (H8085, H1964, H6963) — from His palace-temple in heaven He heard — ve-shavati le-phanav tavo be-oznav (H7775, H6440, H935, H241): the cry came before Him, INTO His ears. Prayer as sound arriving at a physical destination.

7.text: Then the earth shook and quaked, and the foundations of the mountains trembled; they shook because He was angry.
7.amp: Then the earth [eretz] shook [gaash] and trembled [raash]; the foundations [mosadah] also of the hills [har] moved [ragaz — quaked] and were shaken [gaash], because He was wroth [charah — burned with anger].
7.notes: The theophany begins: va-tigash va-tirash ha-aretz (H1607, H7493, H776) — the earth heaves and quakes — u-mosede harim yirgazu (H4146, H2022, H7264), the mountains' foundations tremble. ki-charah lo (H2734): because He burned. Sinai's earthquake (cf. Exodus 19:18) as the response to one man's cry.

8.text: Smoke went up from His nostrils, and devouring fire from His mouth; coals were set ablaze by it.
8.amp: There went up [alah] a smoke [ashan] out of His nostrils ['by his, etc', aph, the KJV margin], and fire [esh] out of His mouth [peh] devoured [akal]: coals [gachelet] were kindled [baar] by it.
8.notes: alah ashan be-appo (H5927, H6227, H639): the nose that is the Hebrew seat of anger, smoking; ve-esh mi-piv tokhel (H784, H6310, H398), devouring fire from the mouth; gechalim baaru mimmennu (H1513, H1197). The imagery is the volcano and the furnace: God's anger at what has trapped His servant, rendered as weather.

9.text: He bent the heavens and came down, with thick darkness under His feet.
9.amp: He bowed [natah — bent, stretched down] the heavens [shamayim] also, and came down [yarad]: and darkness [araphel — thick cloud-darkness] was under His feet [regel].
9.notes: va-yet shamayim va-yerad (H5186, H8064, H3381): the sky bent like a bow and God descended — va-araphel tachat raglav (H6205, H7272): the araphel, Sinai's thick darkness (cf. Exodus 20:21), under His feet. The descent to rescue David is told in the vocabulary of the descent at Sinai.

10.text: He rode upon a cherub and flew; He swooped on the wings of the wind.
10.amp: And He rode [rakab] upon a cherub [kerub], and did fly [uph]: yea, He did fly [daah — swooped, darted] upon the wings [kanaph] of the wind [ruach].
10.notes: va-yirkab al-kerub va-yaoph (H7392, H3742, H5774): God mounted on a cherub, one of the living throne-bearers of Ezekiel 1 — va-yede al-kanphe-ruach (H1675, H3671, H7307), daah being the swoop of a bird of prey (cf. Deuteronomy 28:49). The Rescuer comes fast.

11.text: He made darkness His hiding place, His canopy all around Him: dark waters, thick clouds of the skies.
11.amp: He made [shith] darkness [choshek] His secret place [sether — hiding place]; His pavilion [sukkah — booth, canopy] round about [sabib] Him were dark [cheshkah] waters [mayim] and thick clouds [ab] of the skies [shachaq].
11.notes: yashet choshek sitro (H7896, H2822, H5643): darkness as God's hiding-place — He is unseen even as He arrives — sevivotav sukkato (H5439, H5521), His sukkah, His booth: cheshkat-mayim, ave shechaqim (H2824, H4325, H5645, H7834), rain-dark water and the thick clouds of the upper sky. The storm is His tent.

12.text: Out of the brightness before Him, His thick clouds broke through, with hailstones and coals of fire.
12.amp: At the brightness [nogah] that was before Him His thick clouds [ab] passed [abar — broke through], hail [barad] stones and coals [gachelet] of fire [esh].
12.notes: mi-nogah negdo (H5051): from the radiance in front of Him — the glory inside the darkness — avav aberu (H5645, H5674), His clouds passed, split, and barad ve-gachale-esh (H1259, H1513, H784) fell. Hail and fire together: the seventh plague on Egypt (cf. Exodus 9:24), now aimed at David's enemies.

13.text: The LORD thundered in the heavens; the Most High sent forth His voice — hailstones and coals of fire.
13.amp: The LORD [YHWH] also thundered [raam] in the heavens [shamayim], and the Highest [Elyon — the Most High] gave [natan] His voice [qol]; hail [barad] stones and coals [gachelet] of fire [esh].
13.notes: va-yarem ba-shamayim YHWH (H7481, H8064): the LORD thundered — ve-Elyon yitten qolo (H5945, H5414, H6963): Elyon, the Most High, Melchizedek's title for God, gives His voice, and the voice is the thunder. barad ve-gachale-esh (H1259, H1513, H784) repeated from verse 12 like the second clap.

14.text: He shot His arrows and scattered them; He hurled out lightnings and threw them into panic.
14.amp: Yea, He sent out [shalach] His arrows [chets], and scattered [puts] them; and He shot out [rabab] lightnings [baraq], and discomfited [hamam — threw into panic, routed] them.
14.notes: va-yishlach chitsav va-yephitsem (H7971, H2671, H6327): arrows sent, enemies scattered — u-beraqim rab va-yehummem (H1300, H7232, H2000): lightnings in quantity, and hamam, the panic-verb of the Red Sea and Gibeon (cf. Exodus 14:24; Joshua 10:10). The lightning IS the arrows; the enemies routed by weather.

15.text: Then the channels of the waters were laid bare, and the foundations of the world were uncovered — at Your rebuke, O LORD, at the blast of the breath of Your nostrils.
15.amp: Then the channels [aphiq] of waters [mayim] were seen [raah], and the foundations [mosadah] of the world [tebel] were discovered [galah — uncovered] at Your rebuke [gearah], O LORD [YHWH], at the blast [neshamah — breath] of the breath [ruach — wind] of Your nostrils [aph].
15.notes: va-yerau aphiqe mayim (H7200, H650, H4325): the seabed's channels seen — the Red Sea's dry floor — va-yiggalu mosedot tebel (H1540, H4146, H8398), the world's foundations uncovered. mi-gaaratekha YHWH (H1606), at Your rebuke, mi-nishmat ruach appekha (H5397, H7307, H639): the breath of the wind of Your nose. Exodus 15:8's 'blast of Your nostrils' — the exodus retold as David's rescue.

16.text: He reached down from on high and took hold of me; He drew me up out of many waters.
16.amp: He sent [shalach] from above [marom], He took [laqach] me, He drew [mashah — drew out of water] me out of many ['great', rav, the KJV margin] waters [mayim].
16.notes: After the cosmos convulses, the point of it all: yishlach mi-marom yiqqacheni (H7971, H4791, H3947) — He reached from the height and TOOK me — yamsheni mi-mayim rabbim (H4871, H4325, H7227): mashah is Moses' name-verb, 'drawn out' (cf. Exodus 2:10). The whole theophany was God's arm going into deep water for one man.

17.text: He snatched me away from my powerful enemy, from the ones who hated me, since they were far stronger than I.
17.amp: He delivered [natsal] me from my strong [az] enemy [oyeb], and from them which hated [sane] me: for they were too strong [amats] for me.
17.notes: yatsileni me-oyevi az (H5337, H341, H5794): the strong enemy — Saul, and all who hated (sane, H8130) — ki-ametsu mimmenni (H553): they were mightier than I. The honest admission at the heart of every thanksgiving: the odds were real.

18.text: They met me head-on in the day of my ruin, but the LORD was the staff I leaned on.
18.amp: They prevented [qadam — confronted] me in the day [yom] of my calamity [ed — disaster]: but the LORD [YHWH] was my stay [mishan — support, staff].
18.notes: yeqaddemuni be-yom-edi (H6923, H3117, H343): they met me head-on in the day of my ruin — va-yehi-YHWH le-mishan li (H4937): the LORD as mishan, the staff a man leans his weight on. Enemies in front; God underneath.

19.text: He brought me out into a wide-open place; He set me free, because He delighted in me.
19.amp: He brought me forth [yatsa] also into a large place [merchab — broad, open room]; He delivered [chalats — drew out, freed] me, because He delighted [chaphets] in me.
19.notes: va-yotsieni la-merchab (H3318, H4800): out of the narrows (v. 6) into the broad place — Psalm 118:5's arc — yechalletseni ki chaphets bi (H2502, H2654): and the reason is not David's usefulness but God's delight. Rescue as an act of pleasure.

20.text: The LORD has rewarded me in keeping with my righteousness; in keeping with the cleanness of my hands He has paid me back.
20.amp: The LORD [YHWH] rewarded [gamal — dealt fully with] me according to my righteousness [tsedek]; according to the cleanness [bor — purity] of my hands [yad] has He recompensed [shub — returned to] me.
20.notes: yigmeleni YHWH ke-tsidqi (H1580, H6664): the section (vv. 20-24) that troubles readers — David claims righteousness. The claim is covenant-loyalty in the Saul years, not sinlessness: he kept his hands clean (bor yadai, H1252, H3027) of Saul's blood twice when he could have taken it (cf. 1 Samuel 24, 26). shub (H7725): God returned to him what he had done.

21.text: For I have kept the ways of the LORD, and have not wickedly turned away from my God.
21.amp: For I have kept [shamar] the ways [derek] of the LORD [YHWH], and have not wickedly departed [rasha — acted wickedly] from my God [Elohim].
21.notes: ki-shamarti darkhe YHWH (H8104, H1870): the roads kept — ve-lo-rashati me-Elohai (H7561, H430): not wickedly departed, the verb being 'to be a rasha', to go over to the guilty side. Loyalty stated as not defecting.

22.text: For all His judgments were before me, and His statutes I did not push away from me.
22.amp: For all His judgments [mishpat] were before me, and I did not put away [sur — remove] His statutes [chuqqah] from me.
22.notes: kol-mishpatav le-negdi (H4941): His rulings kept in view — ve-chuqqotav lo-asir menni (H2708, H5493): His statutes not pushed aside. Psalm 119's posture in two lines.

23.text: I was blameless before Him, and I kept myself from my own iniquity.
23.amp: I was also upright [tamim — whole, blameless] before ['with', the KJV margin] Him, and I kept [shamar] myself from mine iniquity [avon].
23.notes: va-ehi tamim immo (H8549): whole WITH Him — the margin's 'with' is the Hebrew — va-eshtammer me-avoni (H8104, H5771): I guarded myself from MY iniquity, the sin he knew he was prone to. Blamelessness here is a man watching his own weak spot, not denying he has one.

24.text: So the LORD has repaid me according to my righteousness, according to the cleanness of my hands in His sight.
24.amp: Therefore has the LORD [YHWH] recompensed [shub] me according to my righteousness [tsedek], according to the cleanness [bor] of my hands [yad] in His eyesight ['before his eyes', ayin, the KJV margin].
24.notes: Verse 20 repeated as a conclusion, with one addition: le-neged enav (H5869) — before His eyes. The cleanness (bor, H1252) that counts is the one God saw, in the cave at En-gedi, when no one else was looking.

25.text: With the faithful You show Yourself faithful; with the blameless man You show Yourself blameless;
25.amp: With the merciful [chasid — the covenant-loyal] You will show Yourself merciful [chasad — act in covenant loyalty]; with an upright [tamim] man [gebar — strong man] You will show Yourself upright [tamam];
25.notes: The law of reciprocity: im-chasid titchassad (H2623, H2616) — with the loyal You act loyally — im-gebar tamim tittammam (H1399, H8549, H8552): with the whole man You are whole. Not that God changes, but that a man's stance toward God determines which face of God he meets.

26.text: with the pure You show Yourself pure; and with the crooked You show Yourself a wrestler.
26.amp: With the pure [barar] You will show Yourself pure [barar]; and with the froward [iqqesh — twisted, crooked] You will show Yourself froward ['wrestle', pathal — twist, grapple, the KJV margin].
26.notes: im-navar titbarar (H1305): pure with the pure — ve-im-iqqesh titpattal (H6141, H6617): and with the twisted, You twist — the margin's 'wrestle' is the root of Naphtali's name (cf. Genesis 30:8). God out-maneuvers the crooked on their own terms; Jacob learned it at the Jabbok.

27.text: For You save an afflicted people, but haughty eyes You bring low.
27.amp: For You will save [yasha] the afflicted [ani — humble, poor] people [am]; but will bring down [shaphel] high [rum] looks [ayin — eyes].
27.notes: ki-attah am-ani toshia (H5971, H6041, H3467): the humble people saved — ve-enayim ramot tashpil (H5869, H7311, H8213): raised eyes lowered. Verses 25-27 are the theology behind verse 19's 'delight': God's delight lands on the lowly.

28.text: For You light my lamp; the LORD my God lights up my darkness.
28.amp: For You will light [or] my candle ['lamp', ner, the KJV margin]: the LORD [YHWH] my God [Elohim] will enlighten [nagah — make shine] my darkness [choshek].
28.notes: ki-attah tair neri (H215, H5216): You light my lamp — 2 Samuel 22:29 has 'You are my lamp'; David himself was called 'the lamp of Israel' (cf. 2 Samuel 21:17). YHWH Elohai yaggiah choshki (H5050, H2822): the darkness God hid in (v. 11) is the darkness He now lights for His servant.

29.text: For by You I can run at a raiding troop, and by my God I can leap over a wall.
29.amp: For by You I have run through ['broken', ruts, the KJV margin] a troop [gedud — raiding band]; and by my God [Elohim] have I leaped over [dalag] a wall [shur].
29.notes: ki-bekha aruts gedud (H7323, H1416): by You I run at a raiding band — the gedud is the Amalekite raiders of Ziklag (cf. 1 Samuel 30) — u-b-Elohai adalleg-shur (H430, H1801, H7791): by my God I vault a wall. Battle-memory told as athletics.

30.text: As for God, His way is perfect; the word of the LORD has been refined in the fire; He is a shield to all who take refuge in Him.
30.amp: As for God [El], His way [derek] is perfect [tamim — whole, without flaw]: the word [imrah] of the LORD [YHWH] is tried ['refined', tsaraph — smelted, the KJV margin]: He is a buckler [magen] to all those that trust [chasah — take refuge] in Him.
30.notes: ha-El tamim darko (H410, H8549, H1870): the way of God is whole — the tamim David claimed for himself (v. 23) belongs to God first. imrat-YHWH tseruphah (H565, H6884): the LORD's word smelted, refined, no dross — Proverbs 30:5 quotes this line. magen hu le-khol ha-chosim bo (H4043, H2620): shield to all who shelter.

31.text: For who is God apart from the LORD? And who is a rock except our God?
31.amp: For who is God [Eloah] save [bilade — apart from] the LORD [YHWH]? or who is a rock [tsur] save [zulah — except] our God [Elohim]?
31.notes: ki mi Eloah mi-balade YHWH (H433, H1107): who is God apart from YHWH? — u-mi tsur zulati Elohenu (H6697, H2108, H430): who is a rock except our God? The rhetorical question is Israel's creed in the negative (cf. Deuteronomy 32:31; Isaiah 44:8).

32.text: It is God who girds me with strength and makes my way perfect.
32.amp: It is God [El] that girds [azar — belts] me with strength [chayil], and makes [natan] my way [derek] perfect [tamim].
32.notes: ha-El ha-meazzereni chayil (H410, H247, H2428): the God who belts me with chayil — the soldier's belt that holds sword and body together — va-yitten tamim darki (H5414, H8549, H1870): and MAKES my way whole. Verse 30's tamim way, given to the servant.

33.text: He makes my feet like the feet of a deer and sets me firm on my high places.
33.amp: He makes [shavah — makes equal, sets] my feet [regel] like hinds' [ayalah — doe, deer] feet, and sets [amad] me upon my high places [bamah — heights, ridges].
33.notes: meshavveh raglai ka-ayyalot (H7737, H7272, H355): feet made like a doe's — the mountain deer that runs sure-footed where a man would fall — ve-al bamotai yaamideni (H1116, H5975), and on my high places He sets me standing. Habakkuk 3:19 borrows the line for the end of his prayer.

34.text: He teaches my hands how to fight, so that my arms bend a bow of bronze.
34.amp: He teaches [lamad] my hands [yad] to war [milchamah], so that a bow [qeshet] of steel [nechushah — bronze] is broken [nachath — pressed down, bent] by mine arms [zeroa].
34.notes: melammed yadai la-milchamah (H3925, H3027, H4421): hands taught for war — skill credited to a Teacher — ve-nichatah qeshet-nechushah zerootai (H5181, H7198, H5154, H2220): a bronze bow bent by my arms, a feat of draw-strength. Psalm 144:1 repeats the first line.

35.text: You have given me the shield of Your salvation; Your right hand has held me up, and Your gentleness has made me great.
35.amp: You have also given [natan] me the shield [magen] of Your salvation [yesha]: and Your right hand [yamin] has held me up [saad — supported]; and Your gentleness ['with thy meekness thou hast multiplied me', anavah — humility, condescension, the KJV margin] has made me great [rabah].
35.notes: magen yishekha (H4043, H3468), the shield of Your salvation; yeminkha tisadeni (H3225, H5582), Your right hand propped me — and then the line the church cannot get past: ve-anvatekha tarbeni (H6037, H7235): Your HUMILITY, Your stooping, has made me great. God's condescension is the source of David's greatness; the Incarnation is this verse at full length (cf. Philippians 2:5-9).

36.text: You have widened the path beneath my steps, and my ankles have not given way.
36.amp: You have enlarged [rachab] my steps [tsaad] under me, that my feet ['mine ankles', qarsol, the KJV margin] did not slip [maad — wobble, give way].
36.notes: tarchib tsaadi tachtai (H7337, H6806): You widened the room for my stride — the merchab of verse 19 under the feet — ve-lo maadu qarsullai (H4571, H7166): and my ankles did not turn. A soldier's gratitude for the small thing: footing.

37.text: I pursued my enemies and overtook them; I did not turn back until they were finished.
37.amp: I have pursued [radaph] mine enemies [oyeb], and overtaken [nasag] them: neither did I turn again [shub] till they were consumed [kalah].
37.notes: erdoph oyevai ve-assigem (H7291, H341, H5381): pursued and caught — ve-lo-ashub ad-kallotam (H7725, H3615): no turning back until finished. The tone shifts: the rescued man is now the pursuer, and the psalm does not apologize for it.

38.text: I struck them down so that they could not rise; they fell beneath my feet.
38.amp: I have wounded [machats — shattered] them that they were not able [yakol] to rise [qum]: they are fallen [naphal] under my feet [regel].
38.notes: emchatsem ve-lo-yukhlu qum (H4272, H3201, H6965): shattered past rising — yippelu tachat raglai (H5307, H7272): fallen under the feet, the ancient posture of victory (cf. Joshua 10:24). David's wars were real wars; the psalm reports them.

39.text: For You girded me with strength for the battle; You made those who rose against me bow down beneath me.
39.amp: For You have girded [azar] me with strength [chayil] unto the battle [milchamah]: You have subdued ['caused to bow', kara, the KJV margin] under me those that rose up [qum] against me.
39.notes: va-teazzereni chayil la-milchamah (H247, H2428, H4421): the belt of verse 32, for the battle — takhria qamai tachtai (H3766, H6965): You made my risers KNEEL under me. Every verb of David's fighting is credited to God's doing.

40.text: You made my enemies turn their backs to me, and I cut off those who hated me.
40.amp: You have also given [natan] me the necks [oreph — back of the neck] of mine enemies [oyeb]; that I might destroy [tsamath — silence, cut off] them that hate [sane] me.
40.notes: ve-oyevai natattah li oreph (H341, H5414, H6203): You gave me my enemies' NAPES — their backs turned in flight — u-mesanai atsmitem (H8130, H6789): and my haters I cut off. The oreph is what a fleeing man shows.

41.text: They cried out for help, but no one came to save them; they cried even to the LORD, and He gave them no answer.
41.amp: They cried [shava], but there was none to save [yasha] them: even unto the LORD [YHWH], but He answered [anah] them not.
41.notes: yeshavveu ve-en-moshia (H7768, H3467): the shava that God heard from David (v. 6) goes unanswered from them — al-YHWH ve-lo anam (H6030), even to the LORD, and He did not answer them. Same cry, same God, different answer: the difference is verse 25's law.

42.text: I crushed them to fine dust before the wind; I poured them out like mud in the streets.
42.amp: Then did I beat them small [shachaq — pulverized] as the dust [afar] before [panim] the wind [ruach]: I did cast them out [ruq — poured out, emptied] as the dirt [tit — mud, mire] in the streets [chuts].
42.notes: ve-eshchaqem ke-aphar al-pene-ruach (H7833, H6083, H6440, H7307): ground to dust the wind carries — ke-tit chutsot ariqem (H2916, H2351, H7324): emptied out like street-mud. The enemy reduced to what feet walk on; the imagery of Micah 7:10.

43.text: You rescued me from the strife of the people; You set me at the head of the nations; a people I had never known now serves me.
43.amp: You have delivered [palat] me from the strivings [rib — contentions] of the people [am]; and You have made [sum] me the head [rosh] of the heathen [goy]: a people [am] whom I have not known [yada] shall serve [abad] me.
43.notes: tephalleteni me-rive am (H6403, H7379, H5971): from the people's quarrels — the civil strife of Saul's house and Absalom's — tesimeni le-rosh goyim (H7760, H7218, H1471): head of the nations, David's empire from Damascus to Edom (cf. 2 Samuel 8). am lo-yadati yaavduni (H3045, H5647): a people I never knew serves me — and the church hears the Gentiles coming to the Son of David.

44.text: At the mere report of me they obey me; the sons of foreign lands come cringing to me.
44.amp: As soon as they hear ['At the hearing of the ear', shema ozen, the KJV margin] of me, they shall obey [shama] me: the strangers ['sons of the stranger', bene nekar, the KJV margin] shall submit ['yield feigned obedience', kachash — cringe, feign, the KJV margin] themselves unto me.
44.notes: le-shema ozen yishameu li (H8088, H241, H8085): at the ear's hearing they hear-and-obey — submission by reputation. bene-nekar yekhachashu-li (H1121, H5236, H3584): the foreigners kachash, the margin's 'feigned obedience' — cringe, fawn: the submission of the conquered, not yet the love of the converted.

45.text: The sons of foreign lands wither away and come trembling out of their strongholds.
45.amp: The strangers ['sons of the stranger', bene nekar] shall fade away [nabel — wither, wilt], and be afraid [charag — tremble] out of their close places [misgereth — enclosures, fortresses].
45.notes: bene-nekar yibbolu (H1121, H5236, H5034): the foreigners wilt like a leaf — ve-yachregu mi-misgerotehem (H2727, H4526): and come trembling out of their walled places. Fortresses opened by fear of a king whose God rides the storm.

46.text: The LORD lives! Blessed be my rock, and let the God of my salvation be lifted high,
46.amp: The LORD [YHWH] lives [chay]; and blessed [barak] be my rock [tsur]; and let the God [Elohim] of my salvation [yesha] be exalted [rum].
46.notes: chai-YHWH (H2416, H3068): the LORD LIVES — against the dead gods of Psalm 115, the living God who answered from His temple. u-barukh tsuri (H1288, H6697), and blessed be my rock; ve-yarum Elohe yishi (H7311, H430, H3468), and let the God of my salvation be lifted high. The war-report gives way to doxology; the titles of verse 2 return.

47.text: the God who gives me vengeance and subdues peoples under me,
47.amp: It is God [El] that avenges ['giveth avengements for', natan neqamah, the KJV margin] me, and subdues ['destroyeth', dabar, the KJV margin] the people [am] under me.
47.notes: ha-El ha-noten neqamot li (H410, H5414, H5360): the God who GIVES vengeances for me — vengeance received, not seized (cf. Romans 12:19) — va-yadber ammim tachtai (H1696, H5971): the verb is dabar, 'to speak' — He speaks the peoples down, subdues by a word; the KJV margin offers 'destroyeth'.

48.text: who pulls me free from my enemies. Yes, You lift me high above those who rise against me; from the man of violence You rescue me.
48.amp: He delivers [palat] me from mine enemies [oyeb]: yea, You lift me up [rum] above those that rise up [qum] against me: You have delivered [natsal] me from the violent ['man of violence', ish chamas, the KJV margin] man.
48.notes: mephalleti me-oyevai (H6403, H341): the escape-maker of verse 2 — aph min-qamai teromemeni (H6965, H7311): raised above the risers — me-ish chamas tatsileni (H376, H2555, H5337): from the ish chamas, the man of violence — Saul, and Absalom, and every one since.

49.text: Therefore I will give You thanks among the nations, O LORD, and sing praises to Your name.
49.amp: Therefore will I give thanks ['confess', yadah, the KJV margin] unto You, O LORD [YHWH], among the heathen [goy], and sing praises [zamar] unto Your name [shem].
49.notes: al-ken odekha ba-goyim YHWH (H3034, H1471): thanks given AMONG THE NATIONS — Paul's proof-text that the Gentiles were always in the plan (cf. Romans 15:9) — u-le-shimkha azammerah (H8034, H2167), and to Your name I will sing praise. The conquered peoples of verses 43-45 are the audience of David's praise, and eventually its choir.

50.text: He gives great victories to His king and shows covenant love to His anointed — to David and to his seed forever.
50.amp: Great [gadal] deliverance [yeshuah] gives He to His king [melek]; and shows [asah] mercy [chesed — covenant love] to His anointed [mashiach], to David, and to his seed [zera] for [ad] evermore [olam].
50.notes: magdil yeshuot malko (H1431, H3444, H4428): magnifying the victories of His king — ve-oseh chesed li-meshicho (H6213, H2617, H4899): doing chesed, covenant love, to His MESSIAH, His anointed — le-David u-le-zaro ad-olam (H2233, H5704, H5769), to David and to his seed forever. The last line is 2 Samuel 7 sung back: the covenant with David's seed forever, which the New Testament opens with (cf. Matthew 1:1; Luke 1:32-33).
